headline: NEUTRAL
headline_tag: Four weeks of steady losses; the label sits just short of BEARISH

action.title: HOLD at planned level
action.detail: Keep marketing and acquisition budgets at the planned level, but do not step them up: Bitcoin is down about 13% in a week and about 21% in a month, a Rally watch drop window has been open since 13 November, and the headline could turn BEARISH if the weakness lasts. Keep a reserve ready instead of cutting, because the long-run base is still rising; spend now on retention, trust and education, and on acquisition only once price closes back above the 200-week average ($68,109) and then the 200-day average ($72,733). This is a budget posture, not trading advice.

analysis: Bottom line: Bitcoin is in a deep, fearful pullback, and today calls for holding steady, not pushing. Short term, the mood is very weak: at about $64,704 Bitcoin has closed under its 50-day average for 28 days in a row, sits about 18% below it and about 23% under its 30-day high, and Fear & Greed reads 11 out of 100. News is pulling this a little lower too, as PANews reports a 1inch warning that an iPhone flaw can steal wallet keys, in a week already full of hacks. A normal week lately swings about $2,957, so a close above $66,250 (the top of a typical week's swing) would turn the week up, a close below $64,150 (the 30-day low) would turn it down further, and in between it stays choppy; safety and explainer messages fit this week far better than promotions.

The next month leans down: the medium-term reading is now just inside its weak zone, but the headline stays NEUTRAL until the model confirms it, while the long-term trend is still up. Price is about 21% lower than 30 days ago and about 11% lower than 90 days ago, and PANews reports Fed official Musalem saying 'several' rate rises may be needed before spring. Bitcoin would have to win back $78,630 (the 50-day average) before the month can firm up, and only above $86,603 (the 90-day high) is there real room to climb. The Fed meeting on 8 December is the next scheduled event; keep bigger campaign pushes until after a clear turn.

The 3-6 month picture still leans up, but only just: the 200-day average is still rising (about 5% over 90 days), while price is about 11% under it and about 48% below its all-time high. The recovery is only back on track if Bitcoin closes above $72,733 (the 200-day average) again; $68,109 (the 200-week average) is the floor price has slipped about 5% under, and $124,753 (the all-time high) stays the far marker. News is adding a little here, as PANews reports the World Bank is testing USDC payments with Citi and Circle, but more weeks under the 200-week average would turn this picture down and be the time to shift budget toward keeping existing users.
